subject: Pilot SLO & MAP: throughput buckets + hosting recommendation
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@shopline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot SLO & MAP: throughput buckets + hosting recommendation

Hi Samir / Asha —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture: 

Summary of customer constraints (what I heard)
- Primary workload: real-time recommendation scoring for product pages (95% of calls are < 1s sessions)
- Target P95 latency: <= 60ms for the inference path (user-perceived time)
- Peak: ~4,000 reqs/s during promotions; steady-state ~600 reqs/s
- Model: 7B transformer with context window ~512 tokens; KV-cache reuse is high (~70% prefix overlap)

Initial recommendation (ops + commercial balance)
- Hosted API: attractive for quick start but will struggle to meet sustained 4k req/s P95 <=60ms without dedicated capacity. Good fallback for bursty, low-commit pilots.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if ShopLine wants a production pilot with consistent P95 under 60ms at 4k req/s; provides GPU reservation, predictable latency, and SLO guarantees.
- Private (VPC): not required for this phase unless procurement demands a private control plane.

Suggested next steps (Mutual Action Plan)
1) Tech validation: SE benchmark on a short synthetic replay (Marissa) — deliver within 3 business days.
2) Proposal: commercial for a 3-month Dedicated pilot including a burst buffer for promotions (Ben) — deliver in 5 business days.
3) Contract/Procurement touchpoint: put contract owner on the loop once proposal is agreed (Samir to confirm).

Attachments: I dropped a rough SLO-options PDF and a MAP spreadsheet for tracking owners and dates.

Can you confirm the peak numbers above (4k peak / 600 steady) and whether you need hard SLA language for the pilot? If yes, we’ll prioritize Dedicated pricing and SLA appendix.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Attachments: shopline_map.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood_slo-options.pdf (PDF stub)

From: Samir Patel <samir@shopline.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Kumar <asha.kumar@shopline.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO & MAP: throughput buckets + hosting recommendation

Thanks Rachel — confirming numbers:
- Peak during promotions: 3.8k–4.2k reqs/s (we typically see short spikes ~10–15 minutes)
- Steady state: 550–650 reqs/s (night & off-peak much lower)
- Latency target: P95 <= 60ms is our goal; P99 can be relaxed to 150ms for now.

We prefer Dedicated for pilot if you can commit to latency SLOs and provide a straightforward pricing path to scale. Procurement prefers a limited SLA during pilot; not a full enterprise contract yet.

I'll loop procurement if needed, but for now please proceed with the tech bench and draft proposal.

—Samir
Head of ML Platforms, ShopLine
samir@shopline.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@shopline.com>, Asha Kumar <asha.kumar@shopline.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T14:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO & MAP: throughput buckets + hosting recommendation

Rachel / Team —

I ran a quick back-of-envelope with the model profile Samir shared in the call: 7B transformer, 512 context, heavy prefix reuse. Key findings: 
- With NVL GPUs and continuous batching + aggressive prefix caching, we can approach ~45–55ms P95 at 600 qps.
- At sustained 4k qps, P95 will depend heavily on batching policy and network concurrency; Dedicated with reserved pool (and tuned batcher) is the safer route to hit <60ms consistently.
- For the short promotional spikes, we recommend configuring a burst pool (Dedicated burst capacity) or a hybrid path that falls back to hosted variants for non-critical requests.

Action items for the bench test (I will run):
- Replay: 30-min window including a 15-min synthetic spike to 4k req/s (need the replay + sample tokens from ShopLine).
- Metrics: collect P50/P95/P99, token-cost, and GPU utilization.
- Deliverable: lab report + recommended batcher/quantization knobs. ETA: 72 hours after we get the sampling data.

I attached a checklist in the spreadsheet. Samir — can you share a 30-min replay (anonymized) and a small set of sample requests? Prefer S3 link or zipped CSV.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot SLO & MAP: throughput buckets + hosting recommendation

Samir — thanks for confirming. Quick commercial note:
- I'll prepare a 3-month Dedicated pilot quote (reserved pool sized for steady 600 qps + bursting to 4k with buffer) and include a pilot SLA appendix (service credits limited to pilot scope).
- Pricing will include a one-time onboarding credit and a discounted pilot rate.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Proposal (with pricing and SOW): 3 business days (by 2026-12-02).
- Trial start: target week of 2026-12-07, assuming replay + contract sign-off.

If procurement will require a PO or an MSA, flag that now and we'll route Legal.
